title: Pomeroy · Connect your AI assistant to Mail, Calendar, Messages and more.
excerpt: Pomeroy connects your AI assistant to Mail, Calendar, Reminders, Notes, Contacts, Messages, Maps, Shortcuts and Weather. Choose which apps it can use. Free to start; $19 once to remove the weekly limit.
content_html:
Connect · Updated 7 September 2026

One menu-bar app holds the macOS permissions and serves your Mac apps over MCP. Any assistant that can start a local MCP server can use it: some in one click, the rest by pasting a configuration Pomeroy writes for you.

Download for Mac

Free for 50 actions a week, shared across every assistant you connect. No account, no card.

Set up with one click

Each of these documents a way in: an extension, an install link, its own command, or a file it reads. Pomeroy uses that way, and the assistant’s own confirmation is the consent step.

  • Claude Desktop

    Anthropic's Mac app

    Pomeroy opens its Claude extension and Claude Desktop asks to install it. No file to find, no Terminal.

    Connect Pomeroy to Claude Desktop

  • Claude Code

    Anthropic's terminal agent

    Pomeroy runs Claude Code's own command to register itself for every project. Start a new session and the tools are there.

    Connect Pomeroy to Claude Code

  • Cursor

    The AI code editor

    Pomeroy opens Cursor's install link. Cursor shows the command and asks you to confirm.

    Connect Pomeroy to Cursor

  • VS Code

    Visual Studio Code with Copilot chat

    Pomeroy opens VS Code's install link. VS Code asks you to trust the server, then starts it.

    Connect Pomeroy to VS Code

  • VS Code Insiders

    The nightly build of VS Code

    Pomeroy opens the Insiders install link. VS Code Insiders asks you to trust the server, then starts it.

    Connect Pomeroy to VS Code Insiders

  • Codex

    OpenAI's agent, in the terminal and ChatGPT

    Pomeroy runs Codex's own command. One registration reaches the Codex CLI, the IDE extension and the ChatGPT desktop app.

    Connect Pomeroy to Codex

  • LM Studio

    Runs models on this Mac

    Pomeroy writes one entry to LM Studio's mcp.json. LM Studio loads it the moment the file is saved.

    Connect Pomeroy to LM Studio

  • Kiro

    AWS's agentic editor

    Pomeroy opens Kiro's install link and Kiro asks to confirm. It picks the server up without a restart.

    Connect Pomeroy to Kiro

  • Cherry Studio

    A desktop client for any model

    Pomeroy opens Cherry Studio's install link and Cherry Studio asks to confirm, twice.

    Connect Pomeroy to Cherry Studio

  • Cline

    The coding agent inside VS Code and JetBrains

    Pomeroy writes one entry to the settings file every Cline surface shares. No restart needed.

    Connect Pomeroy to Cline

  • AnythingLLM

    A private desktop chat app

    Pomeroy writes one entry to AnythingLLM's server file. Press Refresh in Agent Skills and it is there.

    Connect Pomeroy to AnythingLLM

  • Gemini CLI

    Google's terminal agent

    Pomeroy runs Gemini CLI's own command with user scope. Run /mcp reload, or start a new session.

    Connect Pomeroy to Gemini CLI

  • GitHub Copilot CLI

    GitHub Copilot, in the terminal

    Pomeroy runs Copilot CLI's own command. The server is available immediately, with no restart.

    Connect Pomeroy to GitHub Copilot CLI

  • OpenCode

    The open-source terminal agent

    Pomeroy runs OpenCode's own command, which covers the terminal tool and OpenCode Desktop together.

    Connect Pomeroy to OpenCode

Set up by pasting a configuration

These have no file Pomeroy can write, or a route nobody has checked on a Mac yet. Pomeroy puts the exact text on your clipboard and says where it goes. When a route is verified, the assistant moves up to one click.

  • Raycast

    The launcher, with AI built in

    Pomeroy copies the three values Raycast asks for. Paste them into Raycast's Install MCP Server form.

    Connect Pomeroy to Raycast

  • ChatWise

    A Mac chat app for any model

    Pomeroy copies the configuration as JSON. ChatWise imports it from the clipboard in one step.

    Connect Pomeroy to ChatWise

  • goose

    Block's open-source agent

    Pomeroy copies a YAML block for goose's config file. Paste it in and start a new session.

    Connect Pomeroy to goose

  • Windsurf

    The editor now called Devin Desktop

    Pomeroy copies the configuration for Windsurf's mcp_config.json. Paste it in and press refresh in the Cascade panel.

    Connect Pomeroy to Windsurf

  • Warp

    The terminal with an agent in it

    Pomeroy copies the configuration for Warp's .mcp.json. Warp also reads Claude Code's setup, so you may already be done.

    Connect Pomeroy to Warp

  • Zed

    The editor, with assistant panels

    Pomeroy copies a context_servers block for Zed's settings.json. Paste it in, and your comments stay yours.

    Connect Pomeroy to Zed

  • Perplexity

    The answer engine's Mac app

    Pomeroy copies the two values Perplexity's Add Connector form asks for. Paste them in and save.

    Connect Pomeroy to Perplexity

  • JetBrains AI Assistant

    AI Assistant inside IntelliJ, PyCharm and the rest

    Pomeroy copies the JSON that JetBrains AI Assistant's As JSON field takes. Paste it once and every JetBrains IDE has it.

    Connect Pomeroy to JetBrains AI Assistant

  • BoltAI

    A native Mac app for any model

    Pomeroy copies the JSON BoltAI's plugin settings take. Paste it and choose Reload Config.

    Connect Pomeroy to BoltAI

  • Msty Studio

    A desktop chat app with a toolbox

    Pomeroy copies the name and the tool configuration Msty Studio's Toolbox asks for.

    Connect Pomeroy to Msty Studio

Or connect to a local address

Everything above works by starting a small program on your Mac. Some assistants cannot do that: one running in a container, or one that takes a URL and nothing else. For those, Pomeroy has an address on this Mac. It is off until you switch it on, it answers only on this Mac, and Pomeroy writes it into the assistant’s own settings, so you do not type it.

You choose how it is guarded

One setting for the whole address, and each choice accepts one thing and refuses the others.

Token, the default
One secret for the address. Pomeroy writes it into every assistant it can reach, and you can read it for anything it cannot: a container, a script, a request made by hand.

Approval
No secret to hand around. The assistant asks for itself, you answer in a Pomeroy window, and it gets its own credential that you can revoke on its own.

Open
Nothing is checked. Anything running on this Mac can ask Pomeroy for your mail and messages. It exists because a container or a runner can genuinely need it, and switching to it asks you first.

Nothing on your network can reach the address, whichever you pick. Why, and what a tunnel does not buy.

What it looks like

The plainest form, for an assistant that takes a URL. Pomeroy fills in the address and, in Token mode, the header.

Containers on Docker Desktop reach it, and so do dev containers. A virtual machine on its own subnet does not. When you need this.

Or start from the app

Each Mac app has its own page: what any assistant can and cannot do in it, and a link for every assistant and app pair.

Using something else?

Any assistant that runs a local MCP server takes this, the plainest form. Pomeroy’s Copy configuration button puts the same text on your clipboard.

Not on this list

claude.ai and Cowork on the web, ChatGPT on the web, and Grok cannot use Pomeroy. They reach only servers on the public internet, and Pomeroy runs none, on purpose. Why that is a stance.

Connected right now

Pomeroy’s menu bar shows which assistants are connected right now, under the name each gives when it connects. The two ways in are guarded differently, and only one of them can ask you first. Which, and why.

Bring the assistant you already use.

Get 50 actions every week. No Pomeroy account or payment card required. Requires macOS 15 or later.

Download for Mac

content_html_zh:
Connect · Updated 7 September 2026

One menu-bar app holds the macOS permissions and serves your Mac apps over MCP. Any assistant that can start a local MCP server can use it: some in one click, the rest by pasting a configuration Pomeroy writes for you.

Download for Mac

Free for 50 actions a week, shared across every assistant you connect. No account, no card.

Set up with one click

Each of these documents a way in: an extension, an install link, its own command, or a file it reads. Pomeroy uses that way, and the assistant’s own confirmation is the consent step.

  • Claude DesktopAnthropic's Mac appPomeroy opens its Claude extension and Claude Desktop asks to install it. No file to find, no Terminal.Connect Pomeroy to Claude Desktop
  • Claude CodeAnthropic's terminal agentPomeroy runs Claude Code's own command to register itself for every project. Start a new session and the tools are there.Connect Pomeroy to Claude Code
  • CursorThe AI code editorPomeroy opens Cursor's install link. Cursor shows the command and asks you to confirm.Connect Pomeroy to Cursor
  • VS CodeVisual Studio Code with Copilot chatPomeroy opens VS Code's install link. VS Code asks you to trust the server, then starts it.Connect Pomeroy to VS Code
  • VS Code InsidersThe nightly build of VS CodePomeroy opens the Insiders install link. VS Code Insiders asks you to trust the server, then starts it.Connect Pomeroy to VS Code Insiders
  • CodexOpenAI's agent, in the terminal and ChatGPTPomeroy runs Codex's own command. One registration reaches the Codex CLI, the IDE extension and the ChatGPT desktop app.Connect Pomeroy to Codex
  • LM StudioRuns models on this MacPomeroy writes one entry to LM Studio's mcp.json. LM Studio loads it the moment the file is saved.Connect Pomeroy to LM Studio
  • KiroAWS's agentic editorPomeroy opens Kiro's install link and Kiro asks to confirm. It picks the server up without a restart.Connect Pomeroy to Kiro
  • Cherry StudioA desktop client for any modelPomeroy opens Cherry Studio's install link and Cherry Studio asks to confirm, twice.Connect Pomeroy to Cherry Studio
  • ClineThe coding agent inside VS Code and JetBrainsPomeroy writes one entry to the settings file every Cline surface shares. No restart needed.Connect Pomeroy to Cline
  • AnythingLLMA private desktop chat appPomeroy writes one entry to AnythingLLM's server file. Press Refresh in Agent Skills and it is there.Connect Pomeroy to AnythingLLM
  • Gemini CLIGoogle's terminal agentPomeroy runs Gemini CLI's own command with user scope. Run /mcp reload, or start a new session.Connect Pomeroy to Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLIGitHub Copilot, in the terminalPomeroy runs Copilot CLI's own command. The server is available immediately, with no restart.Connect Pomeroy to GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCodeThe open-source terminal agentPomeroy runs OpenCode's own command, which covers the terminal tool and OpenCode Desktop together.Connect Pomeroy to OpenCode

Set up by pasting a configuration

These have no file Pomeroy can write, or a route nobody has checked on a Mac yet. Pomeroy puts the exact text on your clipboard and says where it goes. When a route is verified, the assistant moves up to one click.

  • RaycastThe launcher, with AI built inPomeroy copies the three values Raycast asks for. Paste them into Raycast's Install MCP Server form.Connect Pomeroy to Raycast
  • ChatWiseA Mac chat app for any modelPomeroy copies the configuration as JSON. ChatWise imports it from the clipboard in one step.Connect Pomeroy to ChatWise
  • gooseBlock's open-source agentPomeroy copies a YAML block for goose's config file. Paste it in and start a new session.Connect Pomeroy to goose
  • WindsurfThe editor now called Devin DesktopPomeroy copies the configuration for Windsurf's mcp_config.json. Paste it in and press refresh in the Cascade panel.Connect Pomeroy to Windsurf
  • WarpThe terminal with an agent in itPomeroy copies the configuration for Warp's .mcp.json. Warp also reads Claude Code's setup, so you may already be done.Connect Pomeroy to Warp
  • ZedThe editor, with assistant panelsPomeroy copies a context_servers block for Zed's settings.json. Paste it in, and your comments stay yours.Connect Pomeroy to Zed
  • PerplexityThe answer engine's Mac appPomeroy copies the two values Perplexity's Add Connector form asks for. Paste them in and save.Connect Pomeroy to Perplexity
  • JetBrains AI AssistantAI Assistant inside IntelliJ, PyCharm and the restPomeroy copies the JSON that JetBrains AI Assistant's As JSON field takes. Paste it once and every JetBrains IDE has it.Connect Pomeroy to JetBrains AI Assistant
  • BoltAIA native Mac app for any modelPomeroy copies the JSON BoltAI's plugin settings take. Paste it and choose Reload Config.Connect Pomeroy to BoltAI
  • Msty StudioA desktop chat app with a toolboxPomeroy copies the name and the tool configuration Msty Studio's Toolbox asks for.Connect Pomeroy to Msty Studio

Or connect to a local address

Everything above works by starting a small program on your Mac. Some assistants cannot do that: one running in a container, or one that takes a URL and nothing else. For those, Pomeroy has an address on this Mac. It is off until you switch it on, it answers only on this Mac, and Pomeroy writes it into the assistant’s own settings, so you do not type it.

You choose how it is guarded

One setting for the whole address, and each choice accepts one thing and refuses the others.

Token, the defaultOne secret for the address. Pomeroy writes it into every assistant it can reach, and you can read it for anything it cannot: a container, a script, a request made by hand.

ApprovalNo secret to hand around. The assistant asks for itself, you answer in a Pomeroy window, and it gets its own credential that you can revoke on its own.

OpenNothing is checked. Anything running on this Mac can ask Pomeroy for your mail and messages. It exists because a container or a runner can genuinely need it, and switching to it asks you first.

Nothing on your network can reach the address, whichever you pick. Why, and what a tunnel does not buy.

Not on this list

Connected right now

Pomeroy’s menu bar shows which assistants are connected right now, under the name each gives when it connects. The two ways in are guarded differently, and only one of them can ask you first. Which, and why.
